Hi Alexandra — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- SDK + auth: your app will call Redwood from a server-side backend (node/java) with per-service keys, and you want KMS integration for customer data separation.
- Routing: need region-aware routing (US primary, EU fallback) and latency-sensitive routing for chat vs. batch classification.
- Structured output & tool calling: want deterministic JSON outputs for claim extraction and a safe way to call internal tools.
- Embeddings / reranker: plan to use embeddings for semantic search and a lightweight reranker for top-k precision.
- Policy: enforce latency/cost policy (primary high-quality model with cost-aware fallback to quantized variant; canary rollout for tuning).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra team to map auth/KMS and region/firewall requirements — propose Mon 7/27 or Tue 7/28.
2) Sandbox access + sample traffic (you provide ~5000 request samples over a week) so we can recommend batching/quantization.
3) PoC plan: start with embeddings + reranker + one routing policy (latency threshold + fallback chain).

I've attached a short proposal and an architecture sketch (redwood-model-routing-proposal.pdf). Dev and Marcus are looped for the deep-dive.

Questions for you before the deep-dive:
- Do you have a preferred KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key vault / other)?
- Any hard latency SLOs for chat (p50 / p95)?
- Is PCI / PHI in scope for the initial PoC?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Thanks for the notes — a few technical clarifications and an initial config sketch below.

KMS / PHI: HSM-backed keys are supported via our Private deployment with KMS/HSM integration. For hosted accounts we offer envelope encryption and can integrate customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) with audit logs; for strict HIPAA requirements we recommend Private or Dedicated with our compliance add-on.

SDK + Auth (recommended server-side flow):
- Use server SDK with API key bound to service role.
- Short-lived session tokens for end-user actions (if you need end-user-level access).
- Example (node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });
  // routing policy reference name: acme-chat-policy

Routing / Policy suggestions:
- Policy: primary model = redwood-rlhf-1 (high quality), fallback = redwood-quant-1 (quantized, lower cost).
- Latency rule: if p95 > 350ms for 5m window, divert new requests to fallback model for N minutes and trigger alert.
- Region routing: prefer us-west for US users; route EU users to eu-central and fall back to us-west if capacity spike.
- Canary: start 10% traffic to primary then ramp to 100% over 48–72h with automated rollback on quality regressions.

Embeddings + reranker approach:
- Generate embeddings with redwood-embed-002; store in your vector DB (we recommend the sample schema in the attached).
- Candidate generation: top-100 by cosine. Rerank using a lightweight cross-encoder model on the candidates (re-ranker hosted as a low-latency endpoint).

Attachments / sandbox:
- We can provision a sandbox project with Dedicated-like routing rules for testing. I’ll send a sandbox invite and a PoC checklist after Marissa confirms.

Useful links:
- Model routing docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/model-routing
- Policy config examples: https://docs.redwood.ai/policy-examples

Happy to cover these items on Tue 7/28 at 11:00am PT.
